Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Strides Pharma Science Limited Q2 FY27 
Earnings Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode 
and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should 
you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then

conference over to Mr. Abhishek. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Abhishek: 
Thank you, Nazneen. Very good morning, and thank you for joining us today for Strides earnings 
call for the second quarter and half year ended September 2026. Today, we have with us Badree, 
Managing Director and Group CEO; and Vikesh, Group CFO, to share the highlights of the 
business and financials for the quarter. 
 
I hope you've gone through our results release and quarterly investor presentation that have been 
uploaded on our website as well as stock exchange website. The transcript for this call will be 
available in a week's time on the company's website. Please note today's discussion may be 
forward-looking in nature and must be viewed in relation to the risks pertaining to our business. 
After the end of this call, in case you have any further questions, please feel free to reach out the 
Investor Relations team.  
I now hand over the call to Mr. Badree to make his opening comments. 
Badree Komandur: 
Thank you, Abhishek. Good morning, good afternoon, and good evening, everyone, and a warm 
welcome to the Strides Q2 and H1 FY '27 Earnings Call. Thank you for joining us and for the 
trust and support so many of you have shown us over the years. As always, I'll begin with the 
overview of the quarter and I'll share an update of our overall FY '28 aspiration followed by our 
U.S. and ex-U.S. business.  
Vikesh will then take you through the financial performance in greater detail. After which we'll 
be happy to take your questions.  
Q2 FY '27 has been a quarter of firsts for Strides. We delivered our highest quarterly revenue, 
and for the first time in our history, our ex-U.S. business became larger than our U.S. business, 
a milestone we had set for FY '28, and I have reached well ahead of the schedule. 
 
Let me share the headlines first. Our overall FY '28 growth aspiration remains intact. Our rest 
of the business is accelerating faster than the U.S. and well ahead of the schedule.  
Let me say that again: our overall revenue ambition for FY28 is firmly in place. What will 
change is the regional mix, with Ex-US now contributing more than the US. Our goal was for 
Ex-US revenue to match the US by FY28, and we have achieved that in Q2 FY27 itself. 
As we highlighted last quarter, we expect H2 to be stronger than H1.  
With this, let me take you through the quarter. I am delighted to report a strong second quarter. 
Revenue for Q2 FY27 reached ₹14,297 million, our highest ever, growing 17% year-on-year

and 13% quarter-on-quarter, led by our Ex-US markets and delivered against a challenging 
macro backdrop. 
Ex-US now contributes about 49% of our revenues, up from 43% in Q2 last year, a clear sign 
that our diversification strategy is delivering. 
Absolute gross margin grew a healthy 13% year-on-year to ₹8,003 million. Gross margin stood 
at 56.0%, compared with 57.8% in Q2 last year and 60.9% in Q1, reflecting higher input costs 
linked to the geopolitical situation. 
EBITDA grew 8% year-on-year to ₹2,509 million, crossing the ₹2,500 million mark in a single 
quarter for the first time, another milestone for Strides. EBITDA margin was 17.6%, compared 
with 19.0% in Q2 last year and 18.2% in Q1, as we absorbed higher material, freight and logistics 
costs linked to the same geopolitical situation. 
We are actively addressing these cost pressures through alternate sourcing, procurement 
initiatives and continuous cost optimisation across the business, and we are confident in our 
ability to manage them. 
Operational PAT grew a strong 12% year-on-year to ₹1,358 million, and Operational EPS rose 
to ₹14.7, from ₹13.2 in Q2 last year. 
 
Before I move to our individual businesses, let me step back and share an update on our FY28 
aspiration, which many of you will have already seen in our presentation. 
Let me begin with our track record, because I think it tells our story better than any words I could 
use. Over the last ten quarters, since Q1 FY25, we have delivered steady and predictable growth 
across our key metrics. Revenue has compounded at about 14%, EBITDA at about 13%, and 
operational PAT at about 41%. This consistency gives us real confidence as we enter the next 
phase of our growth. 
We had shared an aspiration of about $375 million in US revenue by FY28. Given how the 
market has evolved, we now expect to reach this a little beyond FY28. The timing has moved; 
the ambition has not. 
Importantly, our overall growth ambition remains fully intact. Our Ex-US business is 
accelerating well ahead of plan, and we expect Strides to sustain its overall top-line growth, 
along with its profitability. 
On the US, the only thing that has moved is the timeline. The business continues to grow, at a 
more measured pace, and the reasons lie in the market rather than in our commitment. A few 
things have changed since we set this aspiration. First, the drug-shortage opportunities in oral 
solids, which lifted the industry at that time, have largely normalised. Second, operating costs 
are higher, with increased material costs and our decision to hold more inventory to sustain our 
industry-leading service levels. We also chose not to launch products that did not meet our 
margin profile, to protect profitability. And third, growth in Controlled Substances is constrained 
by quota allocations, which we expect to improve progressively.

Our response is rooted in our core business philosophy and rests on three pillars. First, 
profitability-led growth. We will protect our established profitability thresholds and drive 
margin-accretive revenues, through selective launches and an expanding set of differentiated 
platforms. We will not compromise on profitability or the quality of our business to chase 
revenue. Second, rebalancing our growth engines, with a sharper focus on Ex-US to drive 
geographical diversification and accelerate overall growth. And third, the US remains a strategic 
growth market for us, with growth anchored in differentiated platforms such as nasal sprays, 
patches and films, and a steadily expanding Controlled Substances portfolio. 
While our US business has remained an anchor for us, the Ex-US business has grown up right 
alongside it. This is where we are seeing real acceleration. Our Ex-US business grew 24% in H1 
FY27. Our goal was for Ex-US revenue to match the US by FY28. Ex-US was at 76% of the US 
in FY25 and 90% in FY26, and in Q2 FY27 it reached 102%, crossing the US well ahead of 
schedule. That is a strategy, patiently pursued for years, coming to life. Ex-US now stands 
shoulder to shoulder with the US, not instead of it but alongside it, and that makes Strides 
stronger as a whole. With growing scale, operating leverage and a better portfolio mix, we also 
expect continued margin expansion in this business. 
As a result, we now have two strong growth engines, both pointed in the same direction. Our US 
business is our foundation, with deep market leadership, a broad approved portfolio and a 
growing pipeline of differentiated and controlled substance products. Our Ex-US business is our 
accelerator, with a strong presence across Europe, the UK, the Nordics and Africa, a robust 
launch engine and a long runway into new territories. Both are powered by the same discipline: 
a deep pipeline, steady launches and a relentless focus on serving our customers. 
These two engines do not compete; they strengthen each other. They give us more ways to grow, 
and make us more diversified and resilient.  
With that, let me take you through our US business. Revenue for Q2 stood at ₹6,855 million, or 
$73 million, growing 9% year-on-year and 9% quarter-on-quarter. For H1, US revenue was 
₹13,137 million, up 7% year-on-year. As we indicated on our last call, we expected a softer first 
half, and I am encouraged by the healthy sequential recovery we delivered this quarter. 
Our B2B partner business saw a strong order book, and we secured meaningful new business 
wins during the quarter, from a partnered product, our recent launches and other key molecules 
in our portfolio. These wins will begin to show up in our performance over the coming quarters 
and underpin the better H2 we have been talking about. 
We continue to deliver industry-leading service levels to all our customers. This is a real 
competitive advantage, and it is central to winning and retaining business with some of the 
largest customers and partners in the market. 
Our portfolio gives us a strong foundation. As of October 2026, we have filed 230 ANDAs, of 
which 212 have been approved, covering 154 products. We also have a basket of approved 
ANDAs yet to be launched, and we will commercialise these at the opportune time. During the 
quarter, we launched three products, taking our commercialised portfolio to 75 products, up from

72 at the end of Q1. We now hold top-three market positions in 38 products, which together 
contribute approximately 70% of our US revenues. 
As I mentioned earlier, our US portfolio is steadily shifting toward higher-margin, differentiated 
products. We have more than 40 value-accretive products in our active pipeline, with filings and 
approvals planned in a phased manner and commercialisation through FY30. 
Controlled Substances is a key part of this strategy, and we see a much larger opportunity ahead. 
Our CS business saw higher customer orders in Q2. Today, our five commercialised CS 
products, all oral solid tablets, contribute about 6% of our US revenue and address a market of 
around $750 million. While this portfolio is constrained by quota allocations, we have more than 
10 CS products in our pipeline across multiple domains, including nasal sprays, patches and 
films, which will expand our addressable market to around $4.5 billion, about six times the 
market we serve today. Importantly, these niche products need only limited API quota, so they 
can drive the ramp-up of this business even within today’s allocations. 
We also hold an advantage that takes years to build. Regulations require these products to be 
manufactured in the US, and our Chestnut Ridge facility already has the capacity and expertise 
to do exactly that. 
Beyond Controlled Substances, we have more than 25 non-CS products to strengthen our core 
portfolio. Together, these products are set to broaden our addressable market, deepen our 
portfolio differentiation and create exciting medium- to long-term growth opportunities. 
Our near-term milestones are already in sight. We continue to invest in building our nasal spray 
portfolio and, as committed on our last call, we filed our third nasal spray, also a controlled 
substance, in September 2026. Our first nasal spray has a GDUFA goal date in H2 FY27, and 
we expect approval in Q4. In Transdermal Patches, we expect to relaunch a controlled-substance 
patch in Q3. This product came to us as part of the ANDAs we acquired from Endo, and we 
expect its full-year benefit to flow into FY28. 
Overall, we expect a better H2 for the US business. We are committed, we are invested, and we 
are building for the long term, growing in a disciplined way that protects the quality of our 
earnings. 
Moving to the Ex-US business, our accelerator, and the most exciting part of our story. Ex-US 
revenue for Q2 reached ₹6,963 million, an outstanding 31% growth year-on-year. For H1, 
revenue was ₹12,838 million, up 24% year-on-year. Importantly, even as Ex-US grew faster 
than the company average, we maintained the profitability of this business. 
What encourages me most is how broad this growth is. Every Ex-US market continues to show 
healthy momentum, driven by new product launches and the expansion of our base business into 
new geographies and with new partners. 
In Q1, we had said that certain shipment delays were a matter of timing, not demand. I am 
pleased to say that, with robust supply chain execution, we delivered Q2 without any spillovers, 
and demand and order books across our key Ex-US markets remain healthy.

In the UK, our prescription business delivered a strong performance, with healthy pricing and 
volume momentum across several key molecules. We continue to deepen our relationships with 
the leading wholesalers in the market, positioning us as a dependable supply partner. We expect 
launch momentum to pick up here and drive the next leg of growth. 
In Europe, our partnered business delivered a strong performance on the back of higher customer 
offtake. Our private label OTC business in Germany continues to grow strongly, with wider 
pharmacy reach and an expanding product portfolio. We are adding new customers across 
several countries, and the multiple new out-licensing deals we signed in the first half will further 
strengthen our momentum. Focused R&D investments and a broader customer base will 
continue to fuel growth in the region. 
The Nordics delivered strong quarter-on-quarter growth, led by our base portfolio. Our branded 
prescription business is showing very encouraging early signs of in-market uptake, with some 
of our branded products now positioned as first-line treatment across several regions in 
Denmark, and more regions expected to follow. Together with increasing launch momentum, 
our branded portfolio is expected to drive growth in the Nordics in the second half. 
In Australia, supply output improved meaningfully, and we have agreed on new projects with 
our key partners, which are now at various stages of implementation. 
In Africa, our branded business in Francophone Africa delivered stellar growth, and we continue 
to outpace the underlying market. Our deal with Sandoz is now awaiting antitrust approval in 
only a few countries, and we expect it to close in Q3. 
In South Africa, we saw strong momentum in the independent pharmacy channel and added new 
products and new business with a leading retail pharmacy chain. 
Overall, with a strong launch pipeline, an expanding customer base and significant regulatory 
filings underway across all our territories, we fully expect the Ex-US business to keep growing 
faster than the company average. 
Before I close, I am delighted to share an important governance update. We are very pleased to 
welcome Mr. Biren Gabhawala to our Board as an Independent Director. Biren is a Chartered 
Accountant with more than three decades of experience in financial reporting, audit, taxation 
and corporate governance, and has chaired the Audit Committees of eClerx Services and 3M 
India. His appointment will further strengthen the Board’s financial oversight, and with it, 
Independent Directors now make up six of our ten Board members. Biren, welcome to Strides. 
Before I hand over to Vikesh, let me leave you with one clear message: our growth story is 
intact. While our US aspiration will take a little longer, our focus on growth is unchanged. We 
will continue to pursue top-line growth across geographies, without compromising on 
profitability. 
Our commitment to the US is equally unchanged. It remains a core market, a central pillar of 
our growth, and home to some of the most exciting opportunities in our pipeline. Our US

business is strong, our Ex-US business is accelerating, and together they give us more ways to 
grow than at any point in our history. 
With that, I will hand over to Vikesh to take you through the financial performance. Vikesh, 
over to you. 
Vikesh Kumar: 
Thank you, Badree. Good morning, good afternoon and good evening, and thank you all for 
joining us. Badree has taken us through the headline performance for the quarter. I will focus on 
the drivers behind our profitability, cash flows and balance sheet metrics.  
Starting with gross margins. Our material costs rose to 44% of revenues in Q2 from 42.2% last 
year, reflecting the increase in raw material costs that Badree described. This moderated our 
gross margins to 56% for Q2. Importantly, for the first half, gross margins stood at a healthy 
58.3%. Our ex-U.S. businesses, where we have maintained profitability even as it scaled, 
continues to support the quality of our margins.  
With cost increases now moderating and our cost improvement programs, including alternate 
sourcing and procurement initiatives gaining traction, we are confident of sustaining our H1 
gross margins going forward. Even in this challenging environment, we remain committed to 
our margin discipline, launching only products that meet our profitability threshold and 
continuing to focus on the quality of our revenue growth. 
 
Our EBITDA for the quarter was INR251 crores, our highest ever at a margin of 17.6%. Higher 
material, freight and supply chain costs linked to the geopolitical situation compressed our 
margins and tempered the flow-through of a very strong revenue growth, but it did not hold back 
the growth in our absolute profitability.  
With the two growth engines, U.S. and ex-U.S. now contributing in balance, our earnings base 
is more diversified and resilient than ever before. On operating costs, other operating costs, 
excluding freight increased by INR47 crores year-on-year due to higher manufacturing and other 
operating costs in manufacturing and freight costs increased INR21 crores year-on-year to 5.5% 
of revenues.  
Even with these cost increases, operating leverage is still visible as total operating costs 
improved by 40 basis points to 38.4% of revenues. In terms of cost line items below EBITDA, 
our depreciation and amortization was at INR57 crores for the quarter and net finance cost was 
at INR43 crores, slightly higher due to the higher average working capital borrowings we had 
during the quarter.  
Operational PAT grew a healthy 11.5% year-on-year to INR136 crores with an operational EPS 
of INR14.7 per share, and our EBITDA to operational PAT conversion remained steady at 54%. 
Reported PAT at INR134 crores for the quarter with a reported EPS of INR14.2 per share. 
 
From a H1 perspective, the first half delivered steady growth across all our key metrics. H1 FY 
'27 revenues grew 15.1% to INR2,695 crores. EBITDA grew 6.9% to INR481 crores with a 
17.8% EBITDA margin and operational PAT grew 9.8% to INR259 crores with operational EPS

of INR28.1 per share. Reported PAT for the first half was at INR300 crores, which was up 26.4% 
and this included the gain on Pivot Path divestment, which we recognized in Q1. 
 
Moving to working capital. Our cash-to-cash cycle stood at 137 days. This is up 13 days from 
March 2026 with absolute working capital increasing by INR307 crores during the first half. 
This reflects 2 components: investment in inventory to counter the elongated supply chain time 
lines and the working capital, which supported our growth.  
Approximately INR174 crores reflects the 14 days increase, which we have seen in our inventory 
levels from Q4. This has been due to the higher transit and lead times due to the geopolitical 
situation, and we also had a deliberate increase in our finished goods inventories at all our front-
end locations. 
This has helped us get back to the industry-leading service levels in a tough operating 
environment. These service levels have been central to the new business wins we secured in the 
U.S. in this quarter and also delivering growth on our ex-U.S. markets. The remaining INR133 
crores increase in working capital is on account of the 15% revenue growth we achieved in H1.  
We remain steadfast in our efforts to continuously improve our cash-to-cash cycle and get them 
back to our historic levels. On net debt, as we had earlier indicated, the inventory build over the 
last 2 quarters was expected to lift our net debt-to-EBITDA ratio temporarily. The ratio now 
stands at 1.72x, reflecting the INR211 crores increase in net debt during H1, driven by working 
capital.  
At the same time, we continue to invest in our future, deploying INR208 crores in capex and 
intangibles to support our growth platforms. Including our nasal spray and transdermal patch 
programs, these investments are directed at the differentiated pipeline Badree outlined, including 
our controlled substances opportunity, which will broaden our addressable market and support 
margin accretive growth. 
 
As inventory normalizes and H2 launches and business wins begins to contribute, we remain 
focused on growth and improving our cash-to-cash cycle. With this, we expect our net debt-to-
EBITDA ratio to stabilize and improve by the end of the year. This net debt is not adjusted for 
the retained investment we hold in OneSource, which is now valued at approximately INR290 
crores.  
On ROCE, our trailing 12-month ROCE was at 14.4%, remaining in the 14% to 15% range. As 
our growth continues and recent investments mature, we expect these returns to improve. To 
summarize, Q2 delivered record revenues and EBITDA in a challenging cost environment and 
the first half saw steady growth across all our key metrics with both our U.S. and ex-U.S. 
business contributing in tandem.  
As we enter the second half, our priorities are clear: build on our growth momentum across these 
markets, preserve our gross margins, improve our cash-to-cash cycle and strengthen our net 
debt-to-EBITDA ratio. With the overall growth aspiration for FY '28 being intact and operating 
leverage playing out, we continue to maintain that bottom line should accelerate ahead of top
